'''Michael Carr''' (also known as Mike Carr; forum handle '''mc9457''') served as Tournament Support Advocate of the [[Players Committee]].

On 2–4 May 2003 he hosted [[2003 Mystic Visions]], a small charity convention in Columbia, Pennsylvania, whose entry-fee and food money went to the Vigilant Fire Company. He signed the announcement as [[Shadow Squadron]] member Shadow 11.<ref name="pc-mv03">[http://www.swccgpc.com/News/Events/2003/mysticvisions05012003.htm Mystic Visions 2003 Weekend is HERE!], swccgpc.com (1 May 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040622063805/http://www.swccgpc.com/News/Events/2003/mysticvisions05012003.htm Internet Archive]</ref> The Players Committee called him "one of the most dedicated volunteers the PC has".<ref name="pc-may03">[http://www.swccgpc.com/Archives/may03archives.htm May Updates], swccgpc.com (1 May 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20031229115404/http://www.swccgpc.com/Archives/may03archives.htm Internet Archive]</ref> In June 2003 he listed The Comic Store in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, as a place where Star Wars CCG was played, with The Adventurers Guild in Harrisburg to follow in July.<ref name="pcf-1757-29245">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=29245#29245 Request for information], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (13 June 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050302002808/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=29226%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

He announced Day of a Thousand Cans, a charity event for several games including Star Wars CCG, held in Lancaster on 17 January 2004; the cans of food donated were given to local food banks.<ref name="pcf-2663-39601">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=39601#39601 Day of a Thousand Cans Is Tomorrow!  Big Prizes!  Charity!], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (16 January 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040326075720/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=2663%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> He also announced the Mystic Visions charity convention of 2004 ([[2004 Mystic Visions]]), then in its fourth year, held from 30 July to 1 August 2004 at the Vigilant Fire Company #2 in Columbia, whose Star Wars CCG Mini-Open qualified two players for Worlds and gave the top finisher the right to help design a virtual card.<ref name="pcf-3515-48081">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=48081#48081 Mystic Visions Is Coming!  (Pennsylvania Charity Convention)], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (25 June 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040901021945/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=51468%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

By October 2004 the Players Committee had introduced him as its new Tournaments Advocate. He described himself as a tournament director for Pennsylvania and a member of [[Shadow Squadron]]. His short-term work would be Worlds 2005 and its qualifying season with [[Nick Kolnik]], with a new ratings system as a longer-term goal. He had played since [[Dagobah]] and had directed tournaments since [[Special Edition]], and he named FreedomCon I, FreedomCon II and Mystic Visions among the events he had planned and run.<ref name="carr">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041013013300/http://swccgpc.com:80/News/MikeBio.htm Meet Michael Carr, New Tournaments Advocate!], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 13 October 2004)</ref>

The August 2005 and May 2006 council pages list him in Strasburg, Pennsylvania.<ref name="council2005">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050829220138/http://www.swccgpc.com/council.htm Advocate Council], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 29 August 2005)</ref><ref name="advocates2006">[https://web.archive.org/web/20060617221233/http://www.swccgpc.com/modules.php?name=Content&pa=showpage&pid=3 Advocates], swccgpc.com Content pid=3 (published 1 May 2006; Wayback, 17 June 2006)</ref>

Late in 2004 he announced lower prices for the PC's tournament prize packages (Ultimate $90, Premiere $45, States $30, Local $20/$10, plus shipping).<ref name="pc-prize04">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041216042725/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Prize_Structure_2004.htm Prizes, Prizes, and More Prizes!], Michael Carr, swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 16 December 2004.</ref>

On 13 October 2004 he announced the Road to Worlds 2005 article, with the new prize packages and fees, and invited tournament directors to apply to run Regionals, Opens, Mini-Opens and State Championships.<ref name="pcf-4042-55074">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=55074#55074 Worlds 2005], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (13 October 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041031162316/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=55081%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> [[David Kangas]] said he had worked with Carr on the [[2005 Endor Regional]].<ref name="pcf-4063-55368">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=55368#55368 State of the PC Address: So long and thanks for all the fish], David Kangas, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (25 October 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050228234323/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=55374%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> Mystic Visions 4.12, held on 11–12 December 2004 at the Vigilant Fire Company #2 in Columbia, hosted the 2005 Coruscant Regional, which gave two byes to Day 2 of the [[2005 World Championship]], the chance to design a virtual card and a guaranteed $100 to first place; entry to the convention was 20 cans of food.<ref name="pcf-4120-56482">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=56482#56482 Mystic Visions 4.12 - December 11, 2004 - 27 Hours of Gaming], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (17 November 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050107081925/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=58042%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In February 2005 he recruited volunteer directors for the PC's Origins 2005 events, from sealed to [[Classic]], Open and [[Secret Squirrel]] side events, saying the PC wanted to "dramatically increase our presence at Origins this year".<ref name="pcf-4429-62756">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=62756#62756 Origins?], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 February 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050226015444/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=60229%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> His forum signature, as captured between October 2004 and February 2005, read "dAgent 80, Shadow 11, SWCCG PC - Tournament Advocate" and promoted Mystic Visions.<ref name="pcf-4042-55074" /><ref name="pcf-4463-60707">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=60707#60707 need help doing tournaments], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (25 January 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050226015125/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=60683%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-4429-61607">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=61607#61607 Origins?], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (3 February 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050226015444/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=60229%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

In April 2005, as Tournament Advocate, Carr offered to set up a sub-committee of the Tournament Advocate, with a head to run it day to day, to administer an online league if enough players were interested. It would need an "official" program for online play, which he expected to be [[Holotable]] unless players felt otherwise; a better rating system than the one he was then testing; and volunteers to set up tournaments, check that they were genuine and handle ratings.<ref name="pcf-5113-69897">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=69897#69897 Online play and Online League], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (18 April 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050430042105/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=70718%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> The same month he wrote that the next virtual set, [[Virtual Set 9: Sanctuary Moon|Virtual Set 9]], was based on a set released after [[Special Edition]] and before [[Death Star II]], and that it had "quite a few player created cards".<ref name="pcf-4954-69274">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=69274#69274 V-9: Speculation Thread], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (11 April 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050426024004/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=69272%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-4954-69275">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=69275#69275 V-9: Speculation Thread], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (11 April 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050426024004/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=69272%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> On 26 April 2005 he ruled as Tournament Advocate that proxies were not tournament legal and would not be while he held the post, unless a card or group of cards cost more than $500 for over a year; for a card that was very hard to get, the Players Committee might instead give some away through a contest with [[DeckTech]] or at tournaments.<ref name="pcf-5220-72142">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=72142#72142 Problems With Proxies], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (26 April 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050429151740/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=72153%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> He added that proxies were not allowed at Players Committee sanctioned events because players could alter their text, that the plan was to print the text of all virtual cards in the coming rules documents, and that he gave away cards from his own collection, almost four complete sets and about 4,000 spare rares, to players who asked and as prize support for local and bigger tournaments.<ref name="pcf-5220-72226">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=72226#72226 Problems With Proxies], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (26 April 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050429151740/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=72153%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

In May 2005, after a player complained about outdated links, he updated the links on swccgpc.com and added links to the Star Wars archives on Decipher's site and to jasonmaas.net/swccg.<ref name="pcf-5457-77804">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=77804#77804 A Question for the masses.], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (18 May 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618064428/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=5457&postdays=0&postorder=asc&start=40 Internet Archive]</ref> On 5 June 2005 he opened a Trade/Collecting Questions thread on the forum, to gather collecting questions in one place and to recreate what had been lost with the old collecting thread, and planned to compile a FAQ from it.<ref name="pcf-5796-81168">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=81168#81168 Trade/Collecting Questions], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (5 June 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618084051/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=81971 Internet Archive]</ref> There he posted notes on the Premiere set of the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]].<ref name="pcf-5796-82926">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=82926#82926 Trade/Collecting Questions], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (14 June 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618084051/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=81971 Internet Archive]</ref> In December 2005 he opened an official Players Committee poll, "Important Poll on Darth Sidious/Emperor Palpatine", to run for a few weeks; its results would be weighed in the final decision.<ref name="pcf-8196-111082">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=111082#111082 Important Poll on Darth Sidious/Emperor Palpatine], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (6 December 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618091245/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=8196&postdays=0&postorder=asc&start=0 Internet Archive]</ref>

On 3 April 2006 he posted the list of players qualified for the [[2006 World Championship]], headed by 2005 winner [[Drew Scott]] and followed by two qualifiers each from the 2006 Kashyyyk, Yavin IV, Alderaan, Coruscant and Bespin Regionals.<ref name="pcf-10256-130633">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=130633#130633 Qualifiers for Worlds 2006], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (3 April 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618055549/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=141112 Internet Archive]</ref> On 6 May 2006 he unlocked the "Road to Worlds 2006" thread and explained why Worlds would not be held at Gen Con. Gen Con charged the Players Committee $1.50 per player for each hour of play, and players also needed a $65–75 pass; with about $2,500 given away in prizes and an average of 30 players per event, a player would have paid at least $102 for a chance to win $100 in the cash consolation event. The PC had chosen Chicago and the store PasTimes, but had not yet confirmed the date with the store; Carr wrote that he had forgotten to tell the PC's contact to request it during his tax season.<ref name="pcf-9457-135624">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=135624#135624 Road to Worlds 2006], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (6 May 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618072946/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=138185&highlight= Internet Archive]</ref> In June 2006 tournament directors who had run V-lite (player-created virtual card) tournaments were asked to e-mail their winners' details to Carr and [[Nick Kolnik]].<ref name="pcf-7309-139829">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=139829#139829 Player-Created Virtual Expansion (aka Virtual Card Lite)], l000needles, quoting Nick Kolnik, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (5 June 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618093240/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=139921&highlight= Internet Archive]</ref> On 15 June 2006 Carr announced that the date of Worlds had changed and that the PC was working with PasTimes on a new one.<ref name="pcf-10323-141302">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=141302#141302 Worlds Date], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 June 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618073156/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=10323&highlight= Internet Archive]</ref> In the same thread he wrote that the location of [[FreedomCon]] had changed three times in two weeks before the PC settled on its venue, without players being told.<ref name="pcf-10323-141343">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=141343#141343 Worlds Date], Michael Carr, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 June 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618073156/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=10323&highlight= Internet Archive]</ref>

He announced the [[2006 Coruscant Regionals]] of 29 April 2006 at Six Feet Under Games in Lancaster, Pennsylvania: six games with a final-four elimination, $10 entry, a guaranteed $100 to first place that rose with attendance, the Players Committee's Ultimate package, and a four-game V-lite consolation event afterwards with a V-lite design for its winner.<ref name="sf-9441-130628">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=130628#p130628 Coruscant Regional & V-Lite Tournament Weekend - 4/29], mc9457 (Michael Carr), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (3 April 2006).</ref> In June 2006, after a dispute over the [[2006 Wisconsin State Championship]], he and [[Nick Kolnik]] ruled that [[Jim Li]] remained Wisconsin State Champion, winner of the Day 2 bye and virtual card designer: a Day 2 bye passed down only if first place already held one, Li did not, and a virtual card design did not pass down.<ref name="sf-10070-143141">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=143141#p143141 Official WI State Championship Post], mc9457 (Michael Carr), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (23 June 2006).</ref><ref name="sf-10070-143098">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=143098#p143098 Official WI State Championship Post], bluethrawn (Nick Kolnik), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (23 June 2006).</ref>
